lesson_title: The Fridge That Counts: Perpetual Inventory
hook_text: R1 500 of stock vanished — and one system spots it while the other calls it 'sales'.
clip_script: Think of a cooldrink fridge with a counter on the door — every bottle in, counted; every bottle out, counted. That is the perpetual inventory system. Every time she sells a pair, two things get written at the till. The customer pays R500 — that is the sale. And the shoes that walked out had cost her R300 — so R300 leaves the stock counter as cost of sales, at the same moment. In December she counts the shelves. The counter says shoes costing R48 000 should be there; her count finds R46 500. That R1 500 gap has a name and demands an answer. Without the counter, the missing shoes would simply look like they were sold — and the loss would hide inside the year forever.
visual_style: A glowing counter ticking on a shop fridge, split-screen till moment showing R500 in and R300 out simultaneously, then a December shelf count flashing a red R1 500 gap.
mood: Clever-gadget energy with a detective payoff.
pacing: Steady build through the counter idea, double-beat on the two till entries, sharp sting on the gap reveal.
